title: Casimir–Polder potential
note: Within a nanometre the potential is the flat-surface, non-retarded −C₃/d³ with C₃ = (ħ/4π)∫α(iξ)(ε − 1)/(ε + 1) dξ; further out retardation and the sphere's curvature weaken it, so the curves part by design: 0.3% at 0.5 nm, 3% at 5 nm, 37% at 50 nm.
summary: the Casimir–Polder potential against its non-retarded limit −C₃/d³
aside:
Close to the surface an atom sees a flat, non-retarded half-space:

$$U(d) \to -\frac{C_3}{d^3}, \qquad C_3 = \frac{\hbar}{4\pi}\int_0^\infty \alpha(i\xi)\,\frac{\varepsilon(i\xi) - 1}{\varepsilon(i\xi) + 1}\,d\xi$$

PyStratify sums the sphere's full retarded response. The two meet within a nanometre (0.3 % at 0.5 nm) and part further out by design, as retardation and the sphere's curvature weaken the potential (37 % at 50 nm).
